title: Pankaj Advani Beats Robert Hall to Win 29th World Title in Billiards
excerpt: Trailing by more than 300 points in the World Billiards Championship final, Pankaj Advani produced a championship-high 587 break to beat Robert Hall 1906-1206 and claim his 29th career world title.
body:
• Pankaj Advani beat England's Robert Hall 1906-1206 in a five-hour final in England to win the WBL World Billiards Championship — his 29th career world title and 21st in billiards.
  • Trailing by more than 300 points with under two hours left, Advani produced a 210 break and then a championship-high 587 break to turn the final decisively.
  • Advani beat Sourav Kothari 1134-575 in the quarterfinals and defending champion David Causier 1607-1271 in the semifinals.
  • India's Shruthi L won the women's title, beating Sweden's Eva Palmius 414-153 to complete a hat-trick of titles. Advani next targets the IBSF World Snooker Championship in Indore in mid-November.

Pankaj Advani clinched his 29th career world title on Thursday, defeating England's Robert Hall 1906-1206 in the final of the WBL World Billiards Championship in England, producing a stunning 587 break to seal the victory.

The 41-year-old from Bengaluru, the only Indian to reach the semifinals, overcame Hall in a gruelling five-hour final at Great Wyrley, according to ANI's report carried by Devdiscourse. The win was Advani's 21st world title in billiards and avenged his loss to Hall in the semifinals of the English Open, a prelude to the championship.

A Final That Turned Late

Hall had reached the World Billiards Championship final five times previously without winning the title, and for long stretches he looked set to end that run. Advani began with a 91 break before Hall responded with a 203 run to take the lead. The two remained close approaching the two-hour mark before Advani produced another century to move ahead.

https://x.com/TheKhelIndia/status/2113332801508655317

Hall then compiled a 331 break to surge more than 300 points clear. At 697-1014, with 115 minutes left on the clock, the Englishman appeared well placed to secure his maiden world title.

"It is an honour and privilege to lift the oldest World Championship trophy in the history of global sport — the John Roberts Trophy. Thrilled to raise my game and make the highest break when I needed it the most in the final after being over 300 points down."

— Pankaj Advani

The 587 Break

Advani responded with a fluent 210 break to cut the deficit to around 100 points. When Hall missed a regulation shot, Advani returned to the table and capitalised with a 587 break — the highest of this year's championship — turning the contest decisively in his favour, according to reporting on the final. He followed it with further runs of 197 and 147.

Advani's breaks of 50 and over in the final were 587, 210, 197, 149, 147, 99, 91, 91 and 55. Hall's were 331, 203, 109, 87, 68 and 50. Hall, gracious in defeat, described the second session as "billiards from the gods" during the prize ceremony, according to reports.

Route to the Title

Earlier in the tournament, Advani defeated compatriot Sourav Kothari, the reigning two-time IBSF world champion, 1134-575 in the three-hour quarterfinal, before overcoming defending champion David Causier 1607-1271 in the semifinals. Hall beat Peter Gilchrist 1029-887 in the other semifinal.

Former world champion Michael Ferreira was absent, having retired from competitive billiards.

Shruthi L Completes Hat-Trick

India completed a double in the women's event. In the five-player women's draw, Shruthi L defeated Eva Palmius of Sweden 414-153 to complete a hat-trick of titles, with breaks of 82, 105 and 57 in the final. Shruthi also competed in the men's division but did not reach the knockout rounds.

What Comes Next

Advani will now switch disciplines and begin preparations for the IBSF World Snooker Championship, scheduled to be held in Indore in mid-November, as he targets his 30th world title. Few athletes in any sport sustain title-winning form across two disciplines for more than two decades; Advani, who won his first world title in 2003 at 18, continues to do so in both billiards and snooker.
